title: Why Do Dogs Go Absolutely Crazy For Treats?
description:

script: The second that treat bag crinkles, your dog turns into a spinning, jumping, drooling mess, and that reaction is bigger than simple hunger. The sound and sight of a treat trigger a genuine dopamine spike in your dog's brain, the same reward chemical involved in anticipation and craving in humans. Dogs also learn through repetition exactly what that crinkle means, so their brain starts the excitement response before the treat even appears, purely from the sound alone. That's actually the same mechanism behind good training, timing a reward correctly rewires behavior fast because the anticipation itself becomes rewarding. So that chaotic treat dance isn't your dog being dramatic, it's pure, uncut dopamine in real time. Want to use that same drive to actually train your dog faster? The link's below.
